rv.q: For those willing to embrace its unvarnished energy, the play offers a uniquely personal – and unexpectedly healing – experience.
I have no doubt of the sincerity of the playwright and admire the commitment of the performers, but I couldn't connect either emotionally or intellectually to anything shown.
In the company’s intimate space, Evans and Klos deliver a poetic and haunting performance filled with laughter and visual spectacle.

I was interested by some ideas onstage, such as the ghost equating herself with her mother and the other queer characters whose existence was rejected, and found the last scene cathartic, but it’s true that the play wasn’t for me.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this bold experimental work exploring faith and queerness in a small town, with some praising its humor and visual spectacle while others find its rough edges and unconventional approach less effective.
